name: unyaffs
desc: Extract files from a YAFFS2 filesystem image
why: Extracts files from YAFFS2 flash images, a real peek into the filesystem inside old Android devices and firmware dumps.

brief.what_it_is: Unyaffs is a small command-line program that extracts files from a YAFFS2 filesystem image, the flash filesystem once common on older Android devices. It takes a YAFFS2 image file as input and writes the recovered files and directories out to disk. According to the Debian package description, it currently only handles images created by mkyaffs2image. The Debian source is ANSI C, about 722 lines plus a 14-line makefile.
brief.why_it_exists: The Debian page gives only the one-line description and does not state a problem or motivation. The scout note frames it as a way to look inside old Android device and firmware dumps.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond a standard package install was visible on the Debian page. It is packaged in Debian (sid version 0.9.7-2, trixie 0.9.7-1), and the Debian package depends on libc6 (>= 2.38). The Debian source package is about 148 kB. The brew formula lists the executable as unyaffs.
brief.standout: It is a narrow, single-purpose tool for one filesystem format, which is an unusual niche to see packaged on its own. The scout note's angle is that it lets you read the contents of old Android and firmware flash dumps without the device.
brief.status: unknown. Debian packaging looks current: sid carries 0.9.7-2, and the Debian copyright file has a 2026 contributor line. The upstream GitHub repository named in the Debian copyright file (github.com/ehlers/unyaffs) returned HTTP 404 when I fetched it, so I could not check upstream commits or releases.
brief.caveats: The Debian description says it can only extract images created by mkyaffs2image, so images from other YAFFS2 writers may not work. The upstream GitHub link returned 404, so the README and project activity could not be read. Copyright is GPL-2+, with Bernhard Ehlers and Kai Wei as upstream authors. The homepage the brew formula points to is the Debian package page, not an upstream project page.
quotes: Unyaffs is a program to extract files from a YAFFS2 filesystem image.
Currently it can only extract images created by mkyaffs2image.
